summary:
I went through all 116 sohzm/cheating-daddy PRs (list in /tmp/cdwin-WinPRs/prs.json, diffs in diffN.patch) and searched upstream/master and upstream/v05 history for Windows-related commits. The fork already has every merged upstream PR except #385. The only upstream-only Windows-related window change, 3cccc36, is matched in the fork. So the gaps are fixes from unmerged PRs and one upstream dependency cleanup (800df4d).

1. Strongest candidate for 'does not work at all' (from source or when building on Windows): the fork added uiohook-napi in 17e6740, and its forge.config.js:30 still has `rebuildConfig: {}`. electron-forge start/package (start.js:60) runs @electron/rebuild. That rebuild only accepts prebuilds named node.napi.node or electron.napi.node (prebuildify.js:47-58). uiohook-napi ships prebuilds/win32-x64/uiohook-napi.node, so the lookup fails and the module is compiled from source with node-gyp. This happened on this Mac too: node_modules/uiohook-napi/build/Release/.forge-meta exists, and build/config.gypi shows runtime=electron, target=44.3.0. On Windows that build needs Visual Studio C++ build tools plus Python, and @electron/node-gyp resolved over git+ssh. Open PR #474 fixes exactly this with `rebuildConfig: { onlyModules: [] }`. The fork does not have it.

2. The screen-capture request handler in window.js:149-156 has no .catch and no empty-sources check, and passes `useSystemPicker: true`. Electron documents that option as macOS 15+ only, so on Windows this handler is always the path that runs. It is also only reached on Windows, because the fork never calls getDisplayMedia on macOS (renderer.js:703-717). Unmerged PRs #431, #298 and #279 fixed it; the fork has none of them.

3. Local-AI mode still uses Whisper `device: 'auto'` (localai.js:184). PRs #298, #315 and #434 report a native ONNX/DirectML crash on Windows with that setting and switched to CPU. The fork does not have this.

The Gemini model/config PRs (#385, #392, #455, #458, #470, #479) mostly do not apply anymore: the fork's own changes replaced them (gemini-3.8-live, gemini-3.8-flash, googleSearch off by default). They cannot explain a Windows-only failure; one leftover, gemma-3-27b-it, is noted below.

findings.title: electron-forge rebuilds uiohook-napi from source, which needs MSVC, Python and git+ssh access to @electron/node-gyp on Windows
evidence: forge.config.js:30 `rebuildConfig: {},` @8c49d85; package.json:39 'uiohook-napi': '^1.5.5' (added in 17e6740)
node_modules/@electron-forge/core/dist/api/start.js:60 calls listrCompatibleRebuildHook(..., forgeConfig.rebuildConfig) on `npm start`; package/make rebuild the same way

node_modules/@electron/rebuild/lib/module-type/prebuildify.js:47-58 only accepts prebuilds/<plat>-<arch>/electron.napi.node | node.napi.node | electron.abiN.node; uiohook-napi ships prebuilds/win32-x64/uiohook-napi.node, so the lookup fails and the module is built with node-gyp (module-rebuilder.js:140-145)
On this Mac the rebuild actually ran: node_modules/uiohook-napi/build/Release/.forge-meta exists, and build/config.gypi has runtime 'electron', target '44.3.0', nodedir ~/.electron-gyp/44.3.0
package-lock.json:695 @electron/node-gyp resolved as git+ssh://git@github.com/electron/node-gyp.git#06b29aa...

Upstream open PR #474 forge.config.js: `rebuildConfig: { onlyModules: [] }` with the comment 'Rebuilding it is unnecessary and breaks on machines without a supported MSVC toolset'; the author then launched the packaged Windows x64 app. https://github.com/sohzm/cheating-daddy/pull/474
module-walker.js:113 + rebuild.js:80: a non-null onlyModules array filters out every module, so [] rebuilds nothing
findings.explanation: On macOS, Xcode command-line tools compile libuiohook silently, so `npm start` works. On a typical Windows machine, `npm install` (uiohook-napi install script `node-gyp-build` finds the prebuild, OK) is followed by `npm start`, and electron-forge then runs @electron/rebuild. That step ignores the prebuild because of its file name and invokes @electron/node-gyp. Without Visual Studio Build Tools (Desktop C++ workload) and Python, it fails with a gyp error and the app never opens. Before that, npm also has to fetch @electron/node-gyp over git+ssh, which fails without a GitHub SSH key or git on PATH. Upstream master avoids all of this because it has no native dependencies after 800df4d. The same rebuild runs during `electron-forge make` for the Squirrel .exe. [INFERENCE] The exact error on the user's Windows machine was not observed.
findings.fix: Set `rebuildConfig: { onlyModules: [] }` in forge.config.js (as in upstream PR #474), or `ignoreModules: ['uiohook-napi']`. Keep uiohook-napi in the asar unpack list. Optionally make the lockfile resolve @electron/node-gyp via https or a registry tarball. Build the Windows .exe on Windows or a windows-latest CI runner.

findings.title: Screen-capture request handler has no error or empty-source handling, so Windows getDisplayMedia can hang and leave the session stuck in 'starting'
evidence: src/utils/window.js:149-156 @8c49d85: `desktopCapturer.getSources({ types: ['screen'] }).then(sources => { callback({ video: sources[0], audio: 'loopback' }); });` with no .catch and no sources.length check, options { useSystemPicker: true }

Electron docs (session.md setDisplayMediaRequestHandler): useSystemPicker is '_macOS_ _Experimental_ … currently available for MacOS 15+ only. If the system picker is available … the handler will not be invoked'; 'loopback … currently only supported on Windows'. https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/docs/api/session.md

Electron issue #45517 (Windows 11): sources[0] undefined -> 'TypeError: video must be a WebFrameMain or DesktopCapturerSource'; a comment reports the share then hangs if the handler throws. https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/45517
renderer.js:703-717: macOS never calls getDisplayMedia (it uses SystemAudioDump); non-mac calls getLoopbackStream -> getDisplayMedia
sessionController.js:43 `await this.operations.startCapture(...)` has no timeout
Unmerged fixes: PR #431 (catch + callback({})), #298 (empty check + catch + useSystemPicker:false), #279 (useSystemPicker:false)
findings.explanation: On Windows, the handler is the only path for system audio and it is never exercised on the Mac. If desktopCapturer.getSources rejects (reported for multi-GPU / DXGI setups in PR #298) or returns [], the callback is never called or throws inside .then. In the hang case, navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia in getLoopbackStream never settles, startCapture never returns, and SessionController stays in 'starting': no audio, no 'Listening'. When getSources does succeed, the code works.
findings.fix: Wrap it as in PR #431: `.then(sources => sources.length ? callback({ video: sources[0], audio: 'loopback' }) : callback(null)).catch(() => callback(null))`. Drop `{ useSystemPicker: true }` or gate it on darwin. Optionally add a timeout around getLoopbackStream so the session still starts with 'Audio unavailable'.

findings.title: Local AI mode: Whisper device 'auto' can natively crash Electron on Windows (DirectML)
evidence: src/utils/localai.js:183-184 @8c49d85: `dtype: 'q8', device: 'auto'`

PR #298 body: "device: 'auto' in loadWhisperPipeline caused ONNX Runtime to attempt DirectML/GPU acceleration on Windows. This is a native crash — it kills the whole process" https://github.com/sohzm/cheating-daddy/pull/298
PR #315 diff: `device: isWindows ? 'cpu' : 'auto'`; PR #434: 'default Whisper to the stable CPU backend instead of automatic DirectML selection'
Upstream issue #239 'local mode crash Windows'
findings.explanation: On macOS, onnxruntime-node 'auto' picks the CPU (or CoreML) provider. On Windows it tries DirectML, and three independent PR authors report a native crash. This only applies if the user selects local mode; BYOK Gemini does not touch localai.js (it is lazy-loaded at gemini.js:38-41).

findings.title: No automatic microphone fallback when Windows loopback yields no audio track
evidence: renderer.js:709-717: a loopback failure only adds a warning; renderer.js:719 requests the mic only when audioMode !== 'speaker_only'
renderer.js:734-736: with no inputs, status 'Audio unavailable — text and Analyze Screen still work'
PR #186 renderer diff: `if (audioMode === 'mic_only' || audioMode === 'both' || !hasSystemAudio)` falls back to the mic
findings.explanation: In the default speaker_only mode, if Windows loopback fails (driver, exclusive-mode device, or the handler issue above), nothing is captured and Gemini never hears a question. On macOS, SystemAudioDump does the capture, so this path is never hit there.
findings.fix: Fall back to getMicrophoneStream when the loopback has no audio track, and show the reason in the status bar.

findings.title: No GPU-sandbox / multi-GPU mitigation for Windows desktop capture
evidence: PR #298: 'Added disable-gpu-sandbox flag on Windows to help with GPU sandbox issues' for DXGI adapter enumeration failures
src/index.js:17-19 @8c49d85: only `disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion` on win32
findings.explanation: On hybrid-GPU laptops, desktopCapturer/getDisplayMedia can fail during DXGI enumeration. This affects both Analyze Screen (screenStill.js uses desktopCapturer) and loopback start. It cannot happen on macOS.
findings.fix: Add app.commandLine.appendSwitch('disable-gpu-sandbox') on win32 only if logs show DXGI or getSources failures. Do not add it pre-emptively.

findings.title: Fork still ships transformers/onnxruntime-node/sharp, which upstream removed in 800df4d
evidence: package.json:36 '@huggingface/transformers': '^3.8.1' (pulls onnxruntime-node with postinstall `node ./script/install`, and sharp with install `node install/check.js || npm run build`)
forge.config.js:7 asar unpack list includes onnxruntime-node, sharp, @img
upstream 800df4d removes @huggingface/transformers and ollama and switches to asar: true
findings.explanation: Neither module is loaded at startup (localai.js:177 is a lazy import), so they do not stop BYOK from launching. But their install scripts are network/native steps that can fail on Windows. Under npm 11 allowScripts they are skipped, which breaks local mode.
findings.fix: Drop @huggingface/transformers if local mode is not needed, or port upstream's native-ai-runtime.js.

findings.title: Retired gemma-3-27b-it still used for the Gemma transcription fallback
evidence: gemini.js:933 model 'gemma-3-27b-it', :954; dispatchTranscription gemini.js:983-987 uses Gemma when there is no Groq key
PR #385 (merged upstream 998a056, not an ancestor of master) renames it to gemma-4-26b-a4b-it; issue #339 404 gemma model
findings.explanation: Not Windows-specific. It only matters on the Groq/Gemma text path, not in the gemini-3.8-live BYOK flow that works on the Mac.
findings.fix: Rename it to gemma-4-26b-a4b-it as in #385 (gemini.js and storage.js:315,335).

openQuestions: What is the exact Windows symptom, and how does the user run it: `npm start` from source on Windows, or an .exe? If the .exe was made on the Mac with `--platform win32`, the uiohook-napi rebuild and the Squirrel maker (needs Wine/Mono) would also fail. Not verified.
Does the Windows machine have Visual Studio Build Tools (C++ workload), Python, and git with a GitHub SSH key? Without them, the rebuild described in finding 1 fails.

In speaker_only mode on the Mac, system audio comes from SystemAudioDump (gemini.js:1554-1571). The renderer AudioWorklet -> 'send-audio-frame' path (renderer.js:650-689, gemini.js:1882-1890) is only used for the Mac mic. The Windows loopback stream at 48 kHz going into AudioContext({sampleRate: 16000|24000}) may therefore never have been tested on any machine. [INFERENCE] Worth a check by the audio-capture investigator.
